newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific may overpay for Pennzoil-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific may overpay for Pennzoil-analysts.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc may end up with egg on its face with its $6.4 billion bid for Pennzoil Co if energy prices decline from their present levels, analysts say.
Union Pacific on Monday said that it would undertake a stock and cash transaction which values Pennzoil at $84 per share, compared with Friday's closing price of 59-5/8.
"This is an acquisition that could look pretty stupid if energy prices fall," said Lyle Brinker, analyst at James Herold.

Union Pacific shares fell 0-3/4 to 25-58 by late morning trade on the day the deal was announced. The company plans to pay $6.4 billion for Pennzoil, split in a cash transaction for 50.1 percent of the shares and a stock deal for the remainder based on a price range for Union Pacific of $25-$30 per share.
"That figure is looking more like $25-$26 per Union Pacific share now," said Brinker.
He noted, however, that if Union Pacific did succeed in extracting more cash flow out of the Pennzoil reserves, and if energy prices remained strong, the deal could look reasonable.
